newsitem.title: MALI: Mali opposition protests peacefully, talks planned.
newsitem.headline: Mali opposition protests peacefully, talks planned.

text.p: Mali's opposition staged a peaceful protest on Monday to back its demands for the suspension of this year's national elections, witnesses said.
President Alpha Oumar Konare has, meanwhile, called talks with opposition leaders for Tuesday to discuss their grievances, officials said.

Witnesses said up to 1,000 militants gathered outside trades union headquarters in Bamako calling for the government to resign, for results of a chaotic April 13 parliamentary election to be scrapped and later polls suspended and reorganised.
Police, who broke up opposition protests last Wednesday, remained in the background.

The April 13 election for a new 147-seat parliament, to be followed by presidential and municipal elections in May and June, are a test of how deeply democracy has taken root in the poor West African nation.
Konare, a historian, was elected during Mali's widely praised 1992 democratic transition and has steered Mali on a course of economic liberalisation.
The opposition has asked the constitutional court to scrap the results of the April 13 poll. Konare has said he will respect the ruling of the court.
The elections are Mali's second multi-party national polls since independence from France in 1960.
Early results from the Independent Electoral Commission (CENI), pointed to a lead for Konare's ruling ADEMA alliance but with many seats needing to go to an April 27 second round.
